subject: Biotechnology
title: Bt Crops
description: A quick win: understand Bt Crops.

hook.text: A soil bacterium makes a crystal protein that kills caterpillars — engineers put that gene into corn and cotton.

buildup.text: Bacillus thuringiensis Cry proteins punch holes in insect guts — harmless to mammals, deadly to target pests.

discovery.text: Bt cotton reduced insecticide spraying in India by 50% — farmer poisoning cases dropped alongside pest damage.

twist.text: Insects evolve resistance — pink bollworm in India developed Bt tolerance in under 15 years of monoculture.

climax.text: Refuge strategies plant non-Bt crops nearby — susceptible insects mate with resistant ones, diluting resistance genes.

punchline.text: A bacterial toxin in every cell — Bt crops fight pests from the inside out.

quiz.question: How do refuge strategies slow insect resistance to Bt crops?
options: They spray extra insecticide on the refuge areas
Susceptible insects from non-Bt refuges mate with resistant ones, diluting resistance genes
They attract natural predators that eat resistant insects

details.summary: Bt crops contain genes from Bacillus thuringiensis that produce insecticidal proteins toxic to specific pest insects. These built-in defenses reduce the need for chemical insecticide sprays and have been adopted on over 100 million hectares globally.
details.whyItMatters: Bt crops have dramatically reduced insecticide use, lowered farmer exposure to toxic chemicals, and increased yields in developing countries. They represent one of the most commercially successful applications of agricultural biotechnology.
takeaways: Bt crops produce insecticidal proteins that kill specific pest caterpillars
They have reduced global insecticide spraying by hundreds of millions of kilograms
Refuge strategies help prevent insects from evolving Bt resistance

faq.question: Are Bt crops safe for humans to eat?
faq.answer: Extensive testing shows Bt proteins are non-toxic to humans because they specifically target receptors in insect guts that mammals lack. Bt proteins are digested like any other protein in the human stomach. Major food safety agencies worldwide confirm their safety.

faq.question: Can insects develop resistance to Bt crops?
faq.answer: Yes, some insect populations have evolved Bt resistance where refuge strategies were not properly implemented. Farmers plant refuges of non-Bt crops to maintain susceptible insect populations, and stacking multiple Bt genes delays resistance evolution.
